originalText:
Someone just built a playable Fruit Ninja game using Claude, Fable 5, Higgsfield MCP, and a single prompt.

Your camera tracks your hand in real time, turning your fingers into the controller as you slice through flying fruit.

What's remarkable isn't the game itself, it's how it was created.

A decade ago, building something like this required specialized hardware, custom software, and a team of developers. Today, AI can generate the experience from a simple idea expressed in natural language.

We're witnessing a fundamental shift in how software gets built.

The distance between imagination and execution has never been shorter.

originalText:
This is the part people don’t show enough about AI game dev on X.

Behind every “Fable 5 made me a full game in one prompt” post, there’s usually a lot of bullshit.

I gave AI a strong /goal:
optimized Three.js grass, chunks, LOD, shader wind.
It produced something.
It understood part of the direction.

But it still missed.
That’s the real workflow.

A prompt can give you a starting point.
It doesn’t magically give you taste, debugging, optimization, and iteration.

You can test the /goal below.
